page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-48 is an arm64-based server instance powered by the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 80 MB of L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 87194.34 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 25168.0, both placing in the top tiers. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 5932.95 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 344.68 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the server demonstrated top-tier performance in Passmark database operations and static web serving throughput, alongside strong Redis SET operations at 102.23 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4a-highmem-48 leverages the ARM architecture to deliver high resource density and memory capacity without the overhead of hyperthreading, as each of the 48 vCPUs maps to a dedicated physical core. However, workloads requiring specialized x86 instruction sets, local NVMe storage, or GPU acceleration are not supported. Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong database and web serving benchmarks, this instance is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, database hosting, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
